title: He thought the fire would destroy him.
paragraphs: He thought the fire would destroy him.

Because deep down, we know what we’ve done.
The hidden thoughts.
The secret habits.
The quiet compromises we dressed up as “normal.”

And then suddenly—
holiness steps into the room.

Not soft.
Not negotiable.
Not watered down.
“Above him stood the seraphim… and one called to another and said: ‘Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts; the whole earth is full of his glory!’” — Isaiah 6:2–3
“Woe is me! For I am lost; for I am a man of unclean lips…” — Isaiah 6:5
That’s the part we don’t post.

The moment when excuses die
and truth stands unfiltered.

Because when real holiness shows up,
it doesn’t just inspire you—

If God is truly holy…
then we are truly in trouble.

Not because He is cruel.
But because He is pure.
“Your eyes are too pure to look on evil…” — Habakkuk 1:13

So Isaiah is undone.
Not dramatic.
Not poetic.

Because he knows—
standing before that kind of fire,
nothing unclean survives.
“Then one of the seraphim flew to me, having in his hand a burning coal… and he touched my mouth…” — Isaiah 6:6–7
That fire… should have finished him.
That coal… came from the altar of sacrifice.
“Behold, this has touched your lips; your guilt is taken away, and your sin atoned for.” — Isaiah 6:7
Here’s the truth most people miss:

God doesn’t pretend your sin isn’t real.
He deals with it… completely.
And He doesn’t cleanse you by lowering His standard.
He cleanses you by providing a sacrifice.

That altar in Isaiah’s vision?
It was pointing forward.
“He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree…” — 1 Peter 2:24

The holiness that should have consumed you…
was poured out on Jesus instead.
That’s why grace is not cheap.
“For our sake he made him to be sin who knew no sin, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.” — 2 Corinthians 5:21
So now the question is not:
Have you been touched by the fire of God’s grace?

After the cleansing—
after the fire—
after the mercy—
“Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” — Isaiah 6:8

And suddenly, the same man who said
“Woe is me…”

Some of you are still running
from the very fire meant to free you.

You think if you get close to God,
He’ll expose you and end you.

And then…
He will redeem you.
You don’t need to clean yourself first.
You don’t need to fix every flaw.
And let Jesus do what you cannot.

Because the same God
who shook the temple in Isaiah 6…

is the same God
who stretched out His hands on the cross.
“If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” — 1 John 1:9
If this convicted you, don’t ignore it.
